classes.name: GlobalHeaderComp
classes.description:
Represents the application header (the top banner), which is present on
every page whether or not a project is open.

This is the entry point for everything **global**: the quick-add ("+") menu
and the "Global modules" menu. Project creation lives here rather than in
`MainMenuComp` — that component is scoped to `.main-menu`, the project
sidebar, which does not exist on /projects/new at all.

It is constructed directly from the page rather than handed out by a page
object, so that it stays usable from any page:

```typescript
test('...', async ({ page, readyOverviewPage }) => {
    void readyOverviewPage;
    const projectsPage = await new GlobalHeaderComp(page).clickProjectsModuleLink();
});
```

Both of its menus render **outside** the banner element (a popover and a
`dialog` on the body), so their contents are located from the page rather
than from the component root.

methods.name: openQuickAddMenu
methods.description: Opens the header's quick-add ("+") menu. Idempotent.
methods.prerequisites: Any page is open and the user is signed in
methods.observableState: The quick-add menu opens, offering "New project", "Invite user" and a work package type per project type

methods.name: clickNewProjectMenuItem
methods.description:
Opens the New project form from the quick-add menu, opening the menu
first if it is closed.

**This route is context-sensitive.** From inside a project the menu item
carries `?parent_id=<that project>` and the form opens with "Subproject
of" pre-filled, so the project created is a *sub*project. For a
guaranteed top-level project use
{@link ProjectsPage.clickNewProjectButton} instead.
methods.prerequisites: Any page is open and the user may create projects
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to /projects/new, with the parent pre-filled when a project was open

methods.name: openGlobalModulesMenu
methods.prerequisites: Any page is open and the user is signed in
methods.observableState: The global modules menu opens, listing Projects, Work packages, Gantt charts and the other global areas

methods.name: clickProjectsModuleLink
methods.description:
Opens the global projects list via Global modules → Projects, opening
the menu first if it is closed.
methods.prerequisites: Any page is open and the user is signed in
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to /projects, the application-wide project list

classes.name: HomePage
classes.description:
Represents the home page of OpenProject.
This page shows WELCOME TO OPENPROJECT section, NEW FEATURES
existing PROJECT and also, allows the user to select a project by
clicking on the `Select a project` link.

methods.name: clickAllProjectsButton
methods.description: Clicks on the 'All projects' button and returns the project selection dropdown.

classes.name: IntroPage
classes.description:
# Page Description
This page represents the introduction screen of the OpenProject application,
where users can log in to the application.

methods.name: fillUserNameTextBox
methods.description: Fills the username text box with the provided text.

methods.name: fillPasswordTextBox
methods.description: Fills the password text box with the provided text.

methods.name: clickOnSignInButton
methods.description: Clicks on the sign-in button and returns a new instance of the HomePage.

classes.name: MainMenuComp
classes.description:
Represents the main menu component in OpenProject on the left of the page.
Allows navigation to different sections like Boards, Time and Costs, Meetings, and Members.

Some modules replace the project menu with their own submenu once opened —
the work packages list, for instance, swaps the project entries for its saved
queries and adds a "Go back one menu level" link. Every navigation method
therefore returns the menu to its project root first, so navigation works
from anywhere in the project.

methods.name: clickBoardsLink
methods.description:
Click on the 'Boards' menu item and returns a BoardsPage.
It will also change the menu to the boards menu. The menu is returned to
the project level first, so this works from inside another module too.
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to the project's boards list and the menu switches to the boards submenu

methods.name: clickTimeAndCostsLink
methods.description:
Click on the 'Time and costs' menu item and returns a CostReportsPage.
The menu is returned to the project level first, so this works from inside
another module too.
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to the project's cost reports page

methods.name: clickMeetingsLink
methods.description:
Click on the 'Meetings' menu item and returns a MeetingsPage.
The menu is returned to the project level first, so this works from inside
another module too.
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to the project's meetings list

methods.name: clickMembersLink
methods.description:
Click on the 'Members' menu item and returns a MembersPage.
The menu is returned to the project level first, so this works from inside
another module too — inside the work packages module, for instance, the
project entries are replaced by that module's saved queries.
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to the project's members list

methods.name: clickWorkPackagesLink
methods.description:
Click on the 'Work packages' menu item and returns a WorkPackagesPage.

Navigates to the work packages list for the currently selected project.
The menu is returned to the project level first, so this works from inside
another module too.
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to the project's work packages list and the menu switches to the work packages submenu

classes.name: OverviewPage
classes.description:
# Overview Page Class
This class represents the overview page in the OpenProject application.
It provides access to the main menu and filtering options.

methods.name: mainMenu
methods.description:
Returns the project's main menu component, used to navigate between modules
(Work packages, Boards, Meetings, Members, Time and costs).
methods.prerequisites: A project overview page is open
methods.observableState: None — returns a component wrapper without interacting

methods.name: getProjectIdentifier
methods.description:
Returns this project's identifier — its URL slug — read from the address
of the page currently open (`/projects/<identifier>`).

This is the cheapest observation of the identifier OpenProject generated
from a project's name: creating a project redirects straight here, and
the slug is in the URL of that redirect. The New project form itself has
no identifier field to read (see `NewProjectPage`), and the stored value
can otherwise only be seen on the change-identifier page.
methods.prerequisites: A project page is open (any URL of the form /projects/:identifier/...)

methods.name: isFilterActive
methods.description:
Checks whether the filter is currently active. Guard calls to
{@link clickActivateFilterButton} with this — that button toggles, so
clicking it while the filter is already active deactivates it.

methods.name: clickActivateFilterButton
methods.description:
Toggles the filter panel. This does not unconditionally activate it — if
the filter is already active the click deactivates it, so guard the call
with {@link isFilterActive}.
methods.observableState: The filter panel toggles; when activated the "Filter by text" textbox becomes available

methods.name: fillFilterByText
methods.description:
Clears the "Filter by text" textbox, types the given text, and waits for
the resulting server query to complete before returning.
methods.prerequisites: The filter panel is active — call {@link clickActivateFilterButton} first
methods.observableState: The results table re-queries and shows only rows matching the text

classes.name: ProjectSelectionDropdownComp
classes.description:
A dialog component with a dropdown for project selection.
Opened from the home page via the 'All projects' button, it lists every
project the user can reach and navigates to the selected project's overview.

methods.name: clickProjectByName
methods.description: Selects a project from the project selection list by its name.
